# Node task_1 — Source/Trigger/Thread flow extraction (read-only research)

Revision for all three sources: `8c32a9dc5d72c033816c6a8110b37f40cf94fba4`, repo `DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype`.
Read via file_read on the four JSON packets in `inputs/projects/project_beta/l2/` (all four read in full; no write to inputs).

## S1 deepseek_readme.json (README.md, 1–39)
- source_sha256 `737997cf5b7d4129f12ed5485ebbdd5e9d2ce3859a82ded6ac535d222327b713`; packet sha256 `3ef5dced147170146cc2b91aca3870cf8bfb84f952a8c16262a7175ab018cfbf`
- L3: research prototype, "not an official DeepSeek product", not production-ready.
- L5: publication-adapted; NOT identical to internal version or to the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*; "Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype."
- L7: proactive coding agent for ONE GitHub repository; listens to GitHub and optionally Feishu; opens a work item, works in its own session+directory, answers in the original conversation (e.g. PR).
- L9: attention-minimizing principle.

## S2 deepseek_philosophy.json (docs/000-philosophy.md, 1–33)
- source_sha256 `0a12126843556fde2bcc2ca52dae2c297b9b5ca9170c3e33d624b2a4d85ca76b`; packet sha256 `2257025548c4799bbda7753936730a80b9f029406c2da08289acb658a40a3c1b`
- L5: take as little human attention as possible.
- L11: acts only when asked or when a written rule allows; request counts only if addressed directly and from an allowed person (allowlist, or an opened conversation); unrequested work requires a team-written rule and starts in record-only mode.
- L12: speaks only when a person must act or can use a result; confirms once; quiet while working; short messages in the originating conversation.
- L19–L20: few concepts / few settings — new business need becomes an attribute of an existing concept or prompt text, not a new concept or setting.

## S3 deepseek_intake.json (src/core/intake.ts, 1–63) — the flow
- source_sha256 `323aadefea69436ba23ed2de3bdbaad673d61915be9e239f3233ecf551a74179`; packet sha256 `d794df820efd11166ef801d30e287a923c16c35dc9e666484be4fad6fdc9bf97`
- L1, L11–14: module = trigger ingestion, thread correlation, subscription fan-out, eval queuing.
- L21: timestamp normalization to canonical ISO before anything else.
- L22: invariant — a trigger must belong to >=1 thread (throws).
- L23: idempotency by trigger id -> `'duplicate'`.
- L25–29: gate is `this.options.scope.scope(trigger)`; not listened -> persist trigger AND a `filtered` disposition with reason code + empty fanout -> `'filtered'`. Note: filtered triggers are still stored (auditability) but never fanned out or evaluated.
- L31, L37: thread correlation is symmetric union of co-occurring thread keys (`thread.correlated`) — derived, not configured.
- L38: fan-out iterates `thread.subscriptions` — subscriptions are per-thread and drive delivery ("subscription pass-through").
- L42–44: `followed` (thread-level context subscription) + `resumes = trigger.human && ticket.ended?.by !== 'human' && !followed`; ended tickets are skipped unless a human message resumes them; a human-stopped ticket receives nothing (mandate withdrawn).
- L45, L51: context-subscription tickets get inputs flagged `context: true` — the worker is told this is ambient context, not a direct ask. Precedence rule: any non-context (own) thread reach flips context false.
- L49–52: input ids are deterministic (`key('input', ticketId, 'trigger', trigger.id)`) — replay-safe fan-out.
- L53–55: disposition record {fanout, context?, at} persisted per trigger.
- L58: only if `this.owners(trigger).length === 0` is the trigger queued for Eval — unclaimed human messages and every bot message get a fallback owner; claimed ones do not.
- L59: wake each fanned-out ticket after persistence.
- L60: emits `trigger.received` for observers.
- Ordering: normalize -> validate -> dedupe -> filter -> save -> correlate -> fan out -> disposition -> eval fallback -> wake -> emit. Pure function of persisted state up to `this.now()` and `scope.scope`.

## Prototype vs architecture article vs unimplemented
- Public prototype (implemented, inspected text): S3 pipeline above; README S1 L7 one-repo GitHub(+optional Feishu) scope; record-only mode for unrequested work per S2 L11.
- Architecture article (*Exploring Super-agent Design*): referenced only by title in S1 L5; its content is NOT in the supplied materials. Anything attributed to it here is a direction, not verified behavior.
- Explicitly unimplemented / not evidenced: per S1 L5 "some designs ... are not implemented in this prototype"; the materials never enumerate which. No multi-repo, no autonomous-initiation path beyond written rules, no evidence of cross-repository or multi-agent topologies. Also no code paths for `followupOwners`, `queueForEval`, `scope`, `Tickets.addInput`, `EnginePart` — only call sites; their internals are unevidenced.
- Non-claim: no execution, build, or test was run; all statements are source-text inspection only.

historical_review_reconstruction.projection: Read-only SELECT projection of constraint_records created_at at or before earliest review.started; no source rows modified or memory database writes.

excluded_later_constraints.statement: do not create work or infer completion from intent.

historical_review_reconstruction.cause: A later read-only Router recap indexed a new workspace-global constraint; current _packet includes it, changing user_constraints and invalidating historical packet/predecessor rechecks. Excluding that later row reconstructs the original review packets without changing their verdicts.

Thread_continuity_reconstruction.limitations: Source delivery to later model turns is verified; semantic understanding is not. Host Router compaction and host relation enumeration do not establish Worker archive recovery.

post_restart_reconstruction.limitations: Source delivery to later model turns is verified; semantic understanding is not. Host Router compaction and host relation enumeration do not establish Worker archive recovery.

diagnostic_conclusions: All seven trigger deliveries have matching consumed inbox rows and exact user transcript messages followed by later assistant turns. The post-restart continuation is user ordinal17 in the original coding run, before assistant19,21,23,25. It was not left in an unpulled inbox.

The only two read_trigger selections are original L3 trigger at assistant3 and pre-restart L3 followup at assistant7. There is no post-restart read of either the new trigger or an old one, and no recall_object selection. No model internal reasoning or causal intent is inferred.

Research L2 receives its followup at user7 and the later integrator receives the same followup at user3. Both proceed to later model turns and deliver without selecting read_trigger for that followup.

Core marks inbox consumed immediately upon transcript insertion. That tracks delivery, not complete source reading. The finalization check for consumed0 cannot detect the delivered-but-unread case; full page/hash/same-run/later-model source proofs remain a separate obligation.

The trusted Core wrapper calls payload Untrusted Core inbox data (not instructions or authority), while a short preview contains a read pointer and continuation requests. This source framing is a concrete affordance/contract boundary, but stored transcript alone does not prove which wording caused a model choice.

A minimal future correction can require complete assigned Trigger context proof, or explicit off-scope handback, before final delivery using bounded feedback and existing budgets. Untrusted payloads must not gain execution authority. This audit adds no runtime gate, alters no PASS, and performs no host substitute reads or live retry.
limitations: Source and receipt integrity and sample content subchecks do not establish semantic truth or general task capability.
Seven independent holdouts are attributed to the original source-bound driver report, not rerun by this auditor.
Later assistant turns and the audited message-loading source establish inclusion in subsequent model context; no captured raw HTTP input or model internal state is claimed.
Host typed relation enumeration and Router archive compaction do not establish actual Worker Recall or Worker archive source recovery; the existing false observations are retained.
SQLite mode=ro/query_only prohibits SQL updates but may involve WAL/SHM bookkeeping. Raw hashes are separately recorded; a physical no-write guarantee is not inferred from query_only.
Historical actual review packet wire savings remain zero. No compression effectiveness is claimed.

Current packet reconstruction is time-sensitive to subsequently indexed global constraints. Exact historical packet agreement uses the explicit read-only constraint frontier projection; current production predecessor revalidation returns false after the later recap constraint.
This supplemental condition is failed and closed. Prior failed conditions and accounting remain preserved; this audit is not a live-call or budget-reset authorization.
